playbook.title: Provisional demonstration playbook
playbook.provenance: Explicit prototype assumptions, not any organisation's policy and not lawyer validated.

rules.title: General confidentiality duration
rules.guidance: General confidentiality should last 3 years after termination; up to 5 years is within the demonstration ceiling. Trade-secret protection may last while information qualifies as a trade secret.
rules.fallback: Consider a period of no more than 5 years, or ask for a matter-specific decision.

rules.title: Use only for the stated purpose
rules.guidance: Use Confidential Information solely to evaluate the stated business relationship. Broader business or product-development use needs judgment.
rules.fallback: Restore the stated-purpose restriction or ask the reviewer to decide.

rules.title: Protection follows retained copies
rules.guidance: Ordinary backup and legally required retention are permitted only while confidentiality and purpose restrictions continue.
rules.fallback: Preserve confidentiality and limited-use protection for retained copies.

rules.title: Read the cap with its exceptions
rules.guidance: General supplier liability capped at fees paid or payable in the preceding 12 months, up to twice that amount. Contractual carve-outs must not create unlimited exposure.
rules.fallback: Bring contractual exceptions within the cap or ask for a decision.

rules.title: Bounded supplier indemnity
rules.guidance: Supplier indemnity limited to third-party IP infringement by the product with exclusions and a defense procedure. Broad breach or first-party indemnities need judgment.
rules.fallback: Narrow the indemnity scope and review its cap treatment together.

rules.title: Known payment period
rules.guidance: Undisputed invoices due in 30 days; up to 60 days is within the ceiling. Missing controlling schedules prevent a conclusion.
rules.fallback: Request the controlling payment schedule or propose no more than 60 days.

context.name: matter-instructions (from the reviewing lawyer)
context.text: Strategic customer. Be flexible on the confidentiality period; hold the residuals carve-outs.

From: Nkechi Okafor <n.okafor@brightwater-analytics.example>
To: Priya Raman <p.raman@helix-instruments.example>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 10:52:11 +0100
Subject: Helix / Brightwater NDA — our markup
Message-ID: <bw-2026-05-19-0931@brightwater-analytics.example>
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

Priya,

Please find attached our markup of the NDA you sent on 4 May (helix-brightwater-nda-v2-bw-markup.docx). Three points, all in track changes:

1. Confidentiality period extended to seven years. Our data sets include clinical-adjacent records held under retention schedules of that length, so a three-year period would leave material unprotected while we are still obliged to hold it.
2. A retention carve-out for backups and compliance copies, since we cannot purge immutable backup media on request.
3. A residuals sentence so that our analysts are not treated as in breach for what they remember.

Happy to discuss any of these on a call.

Kind regards,
Nkechi Okafor
Senior Legal Counsel, Brightwater Analytics Ltd

From: Nkechi Okafor <n.okafor@brightwater-analytics.example>
To: Priya Raman <p.raman@helix-instruments.example>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:03:40 +0100
Subject: Re: Helix / Brightwater NDA — our markup
Message-ID: <bw-2026-05-20-1503@brightwater-analytics.example>
In-Reply-To: <bw-2026-05-19-0931@brightwater-analytics.example>
References: <bw-2026-05-19-0931@brightwater-analytics.example>
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

Priya,

Following our call: on the seven-year point, we could live with five years if the trade-secret tail stays as drafted. Seven was our opening position, not a requirement. The retention carve-out is the one we cannot move on because of the backup media.

Nkechi
